meta.purpose: Should Brightwork launch Dispatch Copilot in Q2 2027, and how should it be packaged and priced to lift net revenue retention from 101% to 105% by 2028 while keeping gross margin at or above 75%?

storyline.governing_thought: Launch Copilot in Q2 2027 inside a Pro tier at $12 more per seat, not as a $149 add-on

exec_summary.text: Copilot is worth launching for productivity; its retention and win-back effects are small

sub_points.text: Beta accounts scheduled 11% more jobs per dispatcher-hour, against 2% for matched ones
AI drives only 6% of churn, and the Routewise win-back is worth at most $0.6M a year

exec_summary.text: Package it in a Pro tier at $12 more per seat, not as a $149 add-on or a free feature

sub_points.text: Only 14% of offered beta accounts bought at $149, against 46% stated intent
Pro at 33% take-up adds about $2.9M; it beats the add-on's best case above 28%

exec_summary.text: Pro meets both financial targets if a usage allowance caps the heaviest accounts

sub_points.text: NRR rises about 5 percentage points if 26% of accounts take Pro; margin holds near 76%

exec_summary.text: Launch in Q2 2027 for the NRR deadline, and hold the mobile delay to two quarters

sub_points.text: Delaying mobile loses more ARR for good if the rewrite would keep over 34% of mobile churners

exec_summary.text: Test Pro on non-beta accounts in Q1 2027, launch in Q2 and manage five measures

sub_points.text: Hold Pro take-up at 26% or more and margin at 75% or more; restart mobile in Q3

next_steps.action: Approve the Q2 2027 launch inside a Pro tier at $12 more per seat, and drop the $149 add-on
Run a randomized test with non-beta accounts: Pro at $12 per seat against the $149 add-on, with a productivity measure
Set the per-seat AI allowance and overage terms, and start the inference contract renegotiation
Fix the mobile rewrite restart for Q3 2027 and report mobile churn monthly
next_steps.owner: Head of Engineering and Head of Customer Success

next_steps.action: Make Pro the default offer in deals where Routewise competes

problem.statement: Should Brightwork launch Dispatch Copilot in Q2 2027, and how should it be packaged and priced to lift net revenue retention from 101% to 105% by 2028 while keeping gross margin at or above 75%?
problem.decision_maker: CEO Maya Okafor and the executive team
success_criteria: Net revenue retention reaches 105% by 2028, from 101% today
Company gross margin stays at or above 75%
The mobile app rewrite slips by no more than two quarters
problem.accuracy: Directional (about ±25%): one beta, one survey and one paywall test
out_of_scope: Adding engineers beyond the 60 in place

one_day_answer.situation: Brightwork has built Dispatch Copilot and run a 12-week free beta; the CPO proposes a $149 add-on worth about $8M of ARR
one_day_answer.complication: The $8M rests on a skewed survey, only 14% bought in the paywall test, Routewise already bundles AI in its Pro plan, and the launch delays the mobile rewrite customers ask for
one_day_answer.resolution: Launch in Q2 2027 inside a Pro tier at $12 more per seat with a usage allowance, then restart the mobile rewrite in Q3 2027

issue_tree.hypothesis: Copilot creates enough customer value and competitive pull to justify a launch
Copilot raises dispatcher productivity across the whole customer base

workplan.analysis: Jobs per dispatcher-hour, beta against matched accounts; beta profile against the base

issue_tree.hypothesis: Copilot lowers churn enough to count in the business case

workplan.analysis: 90-day renewal, beta against matched; main churn reasons

issue_tree.hypothesis: Without AI, Brightwork keeps losing about a third of its contested deals to Routewise

workplan.analysis: Company gross margin with inference for every account

issue_tree.label: Economics
issue_tree.hypothesis: Copilot in a Pro tier meets the 105% NRR target and the 75% gross margin floor
Pro lifts NRR by at least the 4 percentage points the target needs

workplan.analysis: NRR lift from Pro; take-up needed to reach 105%

issue_tree.hypothesis: Company gross margin stays at or above 75% with Pro at any likely usage

finding.note: About 76% at mean usage, but heavy users would push it below 75% without a per-seat allowance

issue_tree.hypothesis: The launch repays its engineering cost within two years

finding.note: About 17 months at full run rate, but about 27 months with a one-year ramp

finding.note: Copilot delay loses about $0.32M of ARR for good and postpones Pro revenue; mobile delay can lose up to $0.94M; the case for Copilot first rests on the 2028 NRR deadline and Routewise

issue_tree.label: More engineers
